expectations.text: Classifies the need as live partner-computed data
expectations.evidence: 'Both examples... are live data computed on the partner's side. That leaves rungs 3-5.'

expectations.text: States that many self-serve apps make per-partner mapping or per-partner schema review (remote schemas or subgraphs) not scale
expectations.evidence: '40 self-serve apps demote rung 3 (you'd write 40 mappings) and rung 5 (you'd review 40 schemas).'

expectations.text: Recommends a single platform-owned mediated extension field (built once, partners plug in behind a published contract) or equivalent for the self-serve case
expectations.evidence: 'Recommendation: rung 4, a mediated extension field... Employee.app(id: ID!)'.

expectations.text: Specifies what the mediated field returns (e.g. a platform-defined envelope plus a validated partner payload, or compares envelope vs JSON scalar vs per-partner union)
expectations.evidence: 'platform-defined envelope: display fields, a link and a status... payload validated against a JSON Schema the partner registers.'

expectations.text: Flags app-registered endpoint URLs as a server-side request forgery risk
expectations.evidence: 'Self-serve endpoint registration is an SSRF door.'

expectations.text: Requires validation of registered URLs: HTTPS public hosts only, blocking private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges, re-checked on DNS resolution or through an egress allowlist
expectations.evidence: 'HTTPS on public addresses only, re-check on every DNS resolution. Reject private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata ranges'.

expectations.text: Flags the shared 60-second response cache as able to serve one user's or tenant's partner data to another
expectations.evidence: 'A partner response without a private scope can be served to a different tenant'.

expectations.text: Requires partner responses to be excluded from the shared cache or keyed per tenant and credential
expectations.evidence: 'Key the cache by partner, tenant, employee and arguments, and mark it private. Turn off cross-request deduplication'.

expectations.text: Rejects showing every app's fields to every tenant; partner data visible only to tenants that installed the app
expectations.evidence: Blocker 3: 'A tenant that hasn't installed app X gets not installed, not X's data.'

expectations.text: Recommends enforcing installs at request time with a platform-assigned scope or policy rather than one schema variant per install combination
expectations.evidence: 'per-install scope the router or proxy checks... one variant per install combination doesn't scale'.

expectations.text: States that no end-user credential is forwarded to apps; a per-app scoped token is used instead
expectations.evidence: 'Forward no client token, cookie or platform API key... Mint a per-partner token per request'.

expectations.text: Requires app endpoints to authenticate calls from the platform and derive tenant from the platform token
expectations.evidence: 'must verify the platform token (mTLS or a signature). It takes tenant and scopes from the token, never from the request body.'

expectations.text: Requires per-app timeouts below the client SLA and a circuit breaker so a slow app degrades to null plus error
expectations.evidence: 'Timeout per partner = client SLA − internal p95... Circuit breaker per partner'; nullable field gives 'null plus an error'.

expectations.text: Classifies the need as live partner-computed data

expectations.text: States that many self-serve apps make per-partner mapping or per-partner schema review (remote schemas or subgraphs) not scale

expectations.text: Recommends a single platform-owned mediated extension field (built once, partners plug in behind a published contract) or equivalent for the self-serve case
expectations.evidence: 'Use `Employee.apps { benefits { … } }`... Define the contract, don't accept any schema.'

expectations.text: Specifies what the mediated field returns (e.g. a platform-defined envelope plus a validated partner payload, or compares envelope vs JSON scalar vs per-partner union)

expectations.text: Flags app-registered endpoint URLs as a server-side request forgery risk
expectations.evidence: 'SSRF: an app can point the gateway at internal hosts.'

expectations.text: Requires validation of registered URLs: HTTPS public hosts only, blocking private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges, re-checked on DNS resolution or through an egress allowlist
expectations.evidence: 'Verify domain ownership, allow HTTPS only. Resolve DNS and block private ranges, pin resolved IP... egress proxy.'

expectations.text: Flags the shared 60-second response cache as able to serve one user's or tenant's partner data to another
expectations.evidence: 'A shared 60s cache will leak data.'

expectations.text: Requires partner responses to be excluded from the shared cache or keyed per tenant and credential
expectations.evidence: 'Key the cache on: (tenant, partner app, employee, caller's effective scopes/role, field set). Never share across tenants.'

expectations.text: Rejects showing every app's fields to every tenant; partner data visible only to tenants that installed the app
expectations.evidence: '"Every tenant sees every app's fields" mixes discovery with authorization.' Resolution requires the tenant to have installed the app.

expectations.text: Recommends enforcing installs at request time with a platform-assigned scope or policy rather than one schema variant per install combination
expectations.evidence: 'enforce at execution and null the field'; 'consent screen with scopes. The gateway enforces it.'

expectations.text: States that no end-user credential is forwarded to apps; a per-app scoped token is used instead
expectations.evidence: 'Never forward the caller's token.' Uses a short-lived Quarrytown-signed JWT.

expectations.text: Requires app endpoints to authenticate calls from the platform and derive tenant from the platform token
expectations.evidence: 'short-lived JWT signed by Quarrytown (JWKS published) with `tenant`, `app` and employee IDs, or use mTLS.'

expectations.text: Requires per-app timeouts below the client SLA and a circuit breaker so a slow app degrades to null plus error
expectations.evidence: 'Make every partner field nullable. Set a hard timeout of about 1–2s per partner, plus a circuit breaker. Return partial data with errors[].extensions.app.'
